t: What Got You Here Won't Get You There
pitch: Twenty interpersonal habits that hold brilliant people back, and a simple method to get rid of them.
center: Changing what holds successful people back
br: Habits in writing and at a distance
one or two · priorities · how others see you
monthly follow-up · suggestions for the future
the disease · the right issue · no ideal
not just managing yourself · team · example
twenty habits · scoring · those around you
quiz: What kind of people does Goldsmith work with?
Successful people whose behaviors hold back their progress
The higher you go, the more obstacles become behavioral rather than technical.
Believing all your behaviors contributed to your success, including the bad ones
People often succeed in spite of certain behaviors, not because of them.
What is the most common habit according to Goldsmith?
The need to win, even on unimportant matters, is the source of many other habits.
What happens when you “add too much value” to a team member's idea?
The idea improves by a few percent, but commitment drops
It is no longer really their idea: often it's better just to say thank you.
Who judges whether change has happened?
The stakeholders who work with them
Other people's perception makes the reality of relationships.
Why announce publicly the behavior you want to change?
Because people see what they expect to see: the announcement draws their attention to your efforts
Perception changes more slowly than behavior.
Very detailed feedback about the past
Asking for two suggestions for the future, listening without commenting and saying thank you
It concerns the future, which can be changed, and involves no personal judgment.
How long does it take for others to perceive real change?
Behavior can change fast, but perception evolves slowly: you must persevere.
